title: Charli XCX will join Madonna on ‘Danceteria’ remix
author: @outinperth, Graeme Watson
body: Madonna and Charli XCX are teaming up for a remixed version of Madonna’s hit Danceteria . The song, which recounts how Madonna got her start in the music industry after persuading DJ Mark Kamins to play her demo tape in a nightclub, has become one of the most popular tracks on her Confessions II album. - Advertisement - Fans have been calling for additional remixes of the song, and Madonna has now revealed that the Afterhours Mix , featuring Charli XCX, will be released on 24 September. So far, the only official reworking of the track has been a remix by DJ Harry Romero. he collaboration was announced in a social media video featuring Madonna repeatedly saying her name and Charli XCX’s. The short clip rapidly cuts between images of both artists dancing. “You wanna talk about Madonna and Charli?” the singer asks before a brief snippet of the new version of the song is played. In the clip, Madonna wears a red hoodie featuring a photograph of herself from the 1980s. Madonna previously teamed up with Sabrina Carpenter for the single Bring Your Love, while Kylie Minogue appeared a reworked version of Love Sensation. Soon, the Madonna will take to the stage at the MTV Video Music Awards, where she has reportedly received 11 nominations. It marks the first time Madonna has led the MTV Video Music Award nominations since 1998, when she released Ray of Light . She also led the nominations in 1990 following the success of Vogue . On both occasions, she received nine nominations, making this year’s total a career best. The VMAs will take place on 27 September in Los Angeles, and there is considerable anticipation surrounding Madonna’s appearance. She has delivered several memorable moments at the awards over the years, including rolling across the stage in a wedding dress at the inaugural ceremony in 1985 and sharing a headline-making kiss with Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.

title: Miley Nearly Hits No. 1 On Her First Visit To A Chart She’s Never Seen Before
author: Hugh Mcintyre, Senior Contributor
body: It's been less than two years since Billboard inaugurated its Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart , a ranking of the most popular tracks that straddle the line between those two styles. For years, pop stars would invade the dance and electronic rankings with massive wins, including stars like Lady Gaga, Beyoncé, Rihanna and more. Then the electronic-leaning tallies began embracing more obscure artists, while the more dance-focused cuts from superstars couldn't find the same footing on pop tallies. Billboard also does not publish some of the same style rosters in the pop field as it does in other genres, as there is no list for pop tunes on streaming sites or general consumption. There is no Hot Pop Songs rundown these days. Miley reaches the Hot Dance/Pop Songs register for the first time and nearly conquers it on her inaugural visit with the first taste of a newly released album. Miley Nearly Rules the Hot Dance/Pop Songs Chart "Bass Persuades" almost rules the Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart as it arrives. The cut – the first single from the newly-released album of the same name – opens at No. 2, bringing Miley into the top 10 and almost to the peak position on her inaugural trip to the tally. Zara Larsson Blocks Miley From No. 1 Miley is blocked from the peak position by Zara Larsson. Her smash "Midnight Sun" is steady at No. 1 for a milestone tenth frame. It is only the fourth track to rule Billboard 's Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart for that length of time. "Bass Persuades" Leads This Week's Debuts The Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart features only 15 spaces, and three of them are occupied by debuts. Miley collects the loftiest of the bunch this time around. Newcomer Adela starts her tune "Boys" at No. 8. Blackpink member Jisoo lands in the lowest rung at No. 15 with a solo tune titled "Click." Miley Debuts Her New Single at No. 2 on Two Charts "Bass Persuades" does not open at No. 1 on any Billboard roster, but it does sit at No. 2 on a pair of them. In addition to the Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart, Miley's latest single comes in second place on the Digital Song Sales tally. On that roster, it trails Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas," which earns a seventeenth stint at No. 1. As "Choosin' Texas" reaches that figure, it matches with "Despacito" by Daddy Yankee, Luis Fonsi and Justin Bieber as the third-longest-running ruler ever. "Bass Persuades" Debuts on Nine Billboard Rankings "Bass Persuades" launches on nine Billboard charts this week, and it's a top 40 hit almost everywhere. The track misses that region on both the Streaming Songs roster and Billboard Global Excl. U.S., but otherwise becomes a quick winner. Miley's latest opens inside the top 10 on three rankings, including its No. 3 start on the Dance Streaming Songs list.
